question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

For a given accelerating voltage Ea and for particular dimensions of CRT, the deflection of the electron beam is _____ to the deflecting voltage.
solution:
The correct answer is __directly proportional****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deflection of the electron beam__ is directly proportional to the deflecting voltage.
 
• This relationship holds true for a given accelerating voltage (Ea) and specific dimensions of the CRT (Cathode Ray Tube).
 
• CRT is used in devices like oscilloscopes, televisions, and radar displays to visualize electrical signals.
 
• The deflection sensitivity of the CRT depends on various factors such as the length of the deflection plates, the distance between the plates, and the accelerating voltage.
 
• To increase the deflection of the beam, either the deflecting voltage can be increased, or the accelerating voltage can be decreased.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **CRT (Cathode Ray Tube):**
 
 
• CRT is a vacuum tube that contains one or more electron guns and a phosphorescent screen.
 
• It works by accelerating and deflecting electron beams onto the screen to produce images.
 
 
 
• **Deflecting Voltage:**
 
 
• The voltage applied to deflection plates to control the path of the electron beam.
 
• Higher deflecting voltage results in greater deflection of the electron beam.
 
 
 
• **Accelerating Voltage:**
 
 
• The voltage that accelerates electrons emitted from the electron gun in the CRT.
 
• Higher accelerating voltage results in a more focused and faster-moving electron beam.
